claim_text: Total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 165,000 in October.
The unemployment rate changed little at 4.1 percent in October.
In October, the number of unemployed people, at 7.1 million changed little.
The unemployment rate has remained in a narrow range of 4.1 percent to 4.3 percent since March.
In October, unemployment rate by group: adult men (3.9 percent).
In October, unemployment rate by group: adult women (3.6 percent).
In October, unemployment rate by group: teenagers (13.9 percent).
In October, unemployment rate by group: White (3.7 percent).
In October, unemployment rate by group: Black (6.6 percent).
In October, unemployment rate by group: Asian (2.8 percent).
In October, unemployment rate by group: Hispanic (4.7 percent).
The number of long-term unemployed (those jobless for 27 weeks or more), at 2.0 million, changed little over the month.
The long-term unemployed accounted for 27.6 percent of all unemployed people.
In October, the labor force participation rate, at 61.9 percent changed little.
In October, the employment-population ratio, at 59.3 percent changed little.
The number of people employed part time for economic reasons increased by 339,000 to 4.8 million in October.
In October, the number of people not in the labor force who currently want a job changed little at 6.0 million.
Among those not in the labor force who wanted a job, the number of people marginally attached to the labor force changed little at 1.6 million in October.
The number of discouraged workers, a subset of the marginally attached who believed that no jobs were available for them, also changed little over the month at 448,000.
Total nonfarm payroll employment had an average monthly gain of 48,000 over the prior 12 months.
Employment in professional and business services increased by 70,000 in October.
Employment in professional and business services: average monthly gain of 15,000 over the prior 12 months.
In October, employment continued to trend up in professional, scientific, and technical services (+33,000).
In October, employment continued to trend up in administrative and support and waste management and remediation services (+28,000).
In October, employment continued to trend up in management of companies and enterprises (+9,000).
Professional and business services has added 269,000 jobs since a recent low in October 2025.
Health care added 42,000 jobs in October.
Health care employment: average monthly gain of 31,000 over the prior 12 months.
In October, employment gains occurred in hospitals (+16,000).
In October, employment gains occurred in home health care services (+11,000).
In October, employment gains occurred in outpatient care centers (+5,000).
In October, transportation and warehousing added 25,000 jobs.
In October, transportation and warehousing growth included couriers and messengers (+17,000).
In October, transportation and warehousing growth included air transportation (+4,000).
Transportation and warehousing added 104,000 jobs since a recent employment low in February.
Since February, transportation and warehousing gains included couriers and messengers (+71,000).
Manufacturing employment continued to trend up in October (+19,000).
Manufacturing employment has increased by 101,000 since a recent low in December 2025.
In October, job gains occurred in computer and electronic product manufacturing (+7,000).
In October, job gains occurred in machinery manufacturing (+4,000).
In October, job gains occurred in primary metal manufacturing (+4,000).
In October, average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls increased by 14 cents, or 0.4 percent, to $38.00.
Over the past 12 months, average hourly earnings have increased by 3.1 percent.
In October, average hourly earnings of private-sector production and nonsupervisory employees rose by 12 cents, or 0.4 percent, to $32.75.
The average workweek for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls remained at 34.4 hours in October.
In October, the manufacturing average workweek was unchanged at 40.5 hours.
In October, manufacturing overtime edged up by 0.1 hour to 3.1 hours.
The average workweek for production and nonsupervisory employees on private nonfarm payrolls declined by 0.1 hour to 33.8 hours.
The change in total nonfarm payroll employment for August was revised up by 53,000, from +133,000 to +186,000.
The change in total nonfarm payroll employment for September was revised up by 31,000, from +29,000 to +60,000.
With these revisions, employment in August and September combined is 84,000 higher than previously reported.
